prompt.context: Our client, Little Bud Co, is a beer company in a small country in Latin America. Little Bud and its main competitor, Geineken, are the only players in the market. Geineken is significantly bigger than Little Bud.
prompt.question: Little Bud's CEO has asked us to provide him with strategic options for the company and a recommendation on what he should do.

clarifying_info.a: What are the goals of any company? The goal is to maximize shareholder value.
The market is mature; growth is low.

clarifying_info.q: How are products sold / what are the distribution channels?
clarifying_info.a: 10% of sales are made through large retailers and 90% through bars, restaurants, and small retailers.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other competitors or market segments to consider?
clarifying_info.a: For the purpose of this case, other competitors can be disregarded. The analysis should be focused on Little Bud and Geineken. The market for small brewers and specialty beers is very small and should be disregarded.

exhibits.title: Revenues per Channel
exhibits.shows: Bar or table showing revenue breakdown by sales channel for Little Bud and Geineken (figures in USD millions)
exhibits.data: Total revenues: Little Bud $100M, Geineken $700M; channel split: 10% large retailers, 90% bars/restaurants/small retailers

exhibits.title: P&L for Little Bud and Geineken
exhibits.shows: Partial P&L table with line items for both companies; Geineken cost figures are left blank for the candidate to fill in
exhibits.data: Little Bud: Revenues $100M, COGS $30M, Gross Profit $70M, G&A $10M, Sales & Distribution $30M, Marketing $25M, EBITDA $5M; Geineken: Revenues $700M, EBITDA $150M (other line items blank)

exhibits.title: Gross Profit Detail — Average Price and Cost Per Unit
exhibits.shows: Table comparing unit price and unit COGS for Little Bud and Geineken
exhibits.data: Little Bud: Unit Price $1.00, Unit COGS $0.30; Geineken: Unit Price $1.10, Unit COGS $0.28

framework: Understand the market: size, growth, channels, competitive landscape
Comparative P&L analysis: revenues, cost structure, and margins for Little Bud vs. Geineken
Identify sources of competitive advantage / disadvantage (scale economies, pricing power, cost structure)
Evaluate strategic options for Little Bud (grow market share, niche/adjacent markets, sell)
Recommend the best option and quantify value via company valuation

questions.prompt: What are the two most important pieces of information you need to start this analysis?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify (1) market size / revenue data and (2) P&L for both Little Bud and Geineken. This frames the scale and margin comparison needed to evaluate competitive position.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 1. What are your initial insights on the market?
questions.guidance: Little Bud has $100M revenues vs. Geineken's $700M — Geineken is 7x larger. The channel mix (90% on-premise / small retail) means distribution efficiency is critical. Both companies sell through the same channels, so scale in distribution matters greatly.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 and the Geineken cost ratios provided, complete the comparative P&L. What are the margins for each player, and what might explain the differences?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate Geineken's cost line items using the provided percentages (G&A 10%, S&D 25%, Marketing 18.1%) and derive EBITDA margin. Key insight: Geineken earns 21.4% EBITDA margin vs. Little Bud's 5.0%. Differences could stem from higher prices, lower costs, or both — candidate should raise the price hypothesis (leading to Exhibit 3) and the cost/scale hypothesis.

math.setup: Apply Geineken cost percentages to $700M revenues to fill the P&L
steps: COGS: $700M x 25.5% = $178M (unit cost $0.28 vs $0.30 for Little Bud)
math.answer: Geineken EBITDA margin = 21.4%; Little Bud EBITDA margin = 5.0%. Geineken has higher gross margin (unit price $1.10 vs $1.00, unit COGS $0.28 vs $0.30) and lower S&D as a % of revenue (25% vs 30%).

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 3. What explains the price and cost differences?
questions.guidance: Geineken charges 10% more per unit ($1.10 vs $1.00), reflecting stronger brand equity from higher marketing spend. Geineken's unit COGS is lower ($0.28 vs $0.30), reflecting purchasing scale with suppliers. On S&D: both use same truck sizes (regulated) and same channels, but Geineken's higher volume means better truck utilization — trucks complete deliveries faster and make more runs, reducing cost per unit.

questions.prompt: What strategic options should Little Bud consider?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm and then evaluate: (1) Increase market share via price war — not viable, Geineken has far more financial firepower; (2) Product innovation — consumer taste is well-defined, no room for new products; (3) Ramp marketing — Geineken already spends 5x more in absolute terms; (4) Cost reduction — already assessed, no further opportunities; (5) Niche/premium beer market — too small in this country; (6) Adjacent markets (sodas, juices) — company has already evaluated this and deemed uncompetitive; (7) Sell the company — the most viable option given structural scale disadvantage.

questions.prompt: How would you value Little Bud? What is its stand-alone market value? What is it worth to Geineken?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose DCF and/or EBITDA multiples. EV/EBITDA = 10x is the given multiple. Stand-alone value = Little Bud's EBITDA x 10x. Value to Geineken = apply Geineken's margin to Little Bud's revenues x 10x (synergy value). Geineken also gains monopoly power, enabling price increases and supplier squeeze — actual value could be even higher.

math.setup: Stand-alone value: Little Bud EBITDA x EV/EBITDA multiple. Value to Geineken: apply Geineken's 21.4% margin to Little Bud's $100M revenues, then apply multiple.
steps: Value to Geineken: $100M x 21.4% = $21.4M EBITDA at Geineken margins; $21.4M x 10x = $214M
Upside: Geineken would become monopoly, further justifying a premium above $214M
math.answer: Stand-alone market value = $50M. Value to Geineken = ~$214M (potentially higher due to monopoly pricing power).

questions.prompt: How can Little Bud maximize the price it receives from Geineken?
questions.guidance: Little Bud should run an open, competitive bid process rather than negotiate bilaterally with Geineken. By signaling that a large international player could enter the market through acquisition, Little Bud creates a credible threat. Geineken has strong incentive to protect its market dominance and prevent a well-capitalized entrant, which should push its offer above $214M.

brainstorming.prompt: What strategic options are available to Little Bud given its structural cost and scale disadvantage?

categories.name: Grow in core market
ideas: Price war to take share from Geineken (not viable — Little Bud lacks financial firepower)
Marketing spend increase (not viable — Geineken spends 5x more in absolute terms)
Product innovation to attract new drinkers (not viable — consumer tastes are set)
Cost reduction to improve competitiveness (not viable — no remaining opportunities identified)

categories.name: Enter adjacent/niche markets
ideas: Premium or craft beer segment (not viable — niche is too small for meaningful growth)
Adjacent beverages such as carbonated soda or juices (not viable — intense competition already assessed)

categories.name: Exit / monetize
ideas: Sell to Geineken via bilateral negotiation
Run open competitive bid process to maximize sale price
Attract international beer conglomerate as competing bidder to force Geineken's hand

recommendation: Little Bud should sell the company. It operates at a structural scale disadvantage — Geineken's 7x revenue base confers lower unit costs, better distribution utilization, and greater marketing firepower that cannot be closed organically.

Little Bud should run an open competitive bid to maximize value. Its stand-alone value is ~$50M, but to Geineken the company is worth ~$214M (or more if Geineken gains monopoly pricing power). A public process incentivizes Geineken to bid aggressively to block international entrants.
risks: Antitrust / competition-authority scrutiny if Geineken acquires and becomes a monopoly
Geineken could respond by initiating a price war to drive Little Bud's value down before an acquisition
International bidders may not materialize, weakening Little Bud's negotiating leverage
next_steps: Hire an investment bank to structure and run the sale process
Evaluate antitrust risk and develop mitigation strategy with legal counsel
Identify any short-term cost savings that could be executed quickly to improve EBITDA (and thus valuation) before the sale
Develop contingency plan for a Geineken-initiated price war during the sale process
